# Embassy v1.8.0 — the same product, one third the size

Two days ago this codebase was 54,399 lines of source. Today it is 18,595 — with two more providers than it had, an open-standard transport, and the failure classes that used to need release-notes apologies made structurally unrepresentable.

The rebuild stands on three primitives. Routes are durable logical identities behind explicit consent edges. Every message lives in one durable attempt state machine — queued, reserved, armed, accepted, terminal — where authorization is the consent linearization point, the first terminal wins, and anything lost after arming settles ambiguous and is never replayed. And transports are small per-operation things: no provider I/O ever runs under the durable commit lane, so a slow model turn cannot starve status reads, observations, or unrelated deliveries — a deterministic 90-second-pause test holds the promise.

Codex delivery is now stateless. Registering a task records an alias and a durable thread ID, nothing else; each delivery freshly attests the managed install, resumes the exact thread, runs one turn, and closes. Restart your daemon, restart your Desktop, restart both — the next dispatch neither knows nor cares. The generation, reactivation, and re-anchor machinery that four releases patched is deleted, not fixed. Claude delivery crosses an exact prepared-frame boundary, one immutable frame consumed exactly once, in the production helper path too. And the Claude launcher attestation is gone entirely: Embassy validates only what it consumes, so Homebrew installs, official installs, and machines with no Claude at all boot the same broker honestly.

Upgrading is one explicit offline step: back up and run `embassy convert-state-v2-to-v3`, then start the new broker. The runtime accepts only v3 state and says exactly why when it meets older bytes.

Verification: 518 tests and the full deliverability soak from cold worktrees; four adversarial review rounds per major slice; frozen byte-held wire contracts for Codex and Claude; every accepted message in a 771-message, two-restart soak settled terminal exactly once.

Upgrade: `npm install -g agent-embassy@1.8.0`, stop the broker, `embassy convert-state-v2-to-v3`, start the broker.
